sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the distinction between Tzion and Yerushalayim as levels of fear of G-d, with Tzion representing higher fear and Yerushalayim lower fear, and their connection to the names Havayah and Elokim.

translations.translation: And this will be understood by prefacing what was said by the Admore"R Mahara"Sh in his maamar beginning "Shivchi"
"Yerushalayim, praise Havayah; laud your G-d, Tzion"
(of Parshas Tavo, one hundred years ago),
that it is necessary to understand,
after all, Tzion is higher than Yerushalayim
[for Tzion is the inwardness of Yerushalayim],
and nevertheless,
regarding Yerushalayim it says Havayah and regarding Tzion it says Elokim.
And behold, Yisrael is called by the name Tzion, as it is stated,
"to say to Tzion, 'You are My people.'"
And based on this, it can be said,
that Tzion and Yerushalayim are two levels within Yisrael.
And according to what is stated in the aforementioned maamar that Yerushalayim is lower fear,
it can be said,
that Tzion is higher fear.
And one can say the hint of higher fear in Tzion,
for the self-nullification of higher fear is nullification of existence,
and this nullification is hinted at in Tzion, from the term "sign," that it has no existence of its own and is only a sign for what is above.
And this is that "from Tzion shall go forth Torah, and the word of Havayah from Yerushalayim,"
that regarding Tzion it says Torah, and regarding Yerushalayim it says word of Havayah,
for among the distinctions between lower fear and higher fear is,
that lower fear is from His greatness in the creation and coming-into-being of the worlds,
that the self-nullification of this fear is the nullification of the yesh (somethingness).
And higher fear is from His greatness and loftiness that is above worlds,
for everything before Him is considered as nothing,
that the self-nullification in this fear is nullification of existence.
And this is what is stated,
"And Havayah commanded us to do all these statutes, to fear Havayah,"
that in order to come to fear Havayah,
higher fear,
which comes through the feeling of the loftiness of Ein Sof that is above worlds,
it is through Torah and mitzvos
(these statutes).
For through contemplation it is possible to attain only the Elokus that is commensurate with the worlds,
and in order for the loftiness of Ein Sof that is above worlds to be felt,
it is specifically through a revelation from above that is drawn down through the study of Torah and the fulfillment of mitzvos.
And this is the connection of Tzion to Torah and of Yerushalayim to the word of Havayah,
for lower fear
(Yerushalayim)
is from the word of Havayah that brings the worlds into being,
"by the word of Havayah the heavens were made,"
and higher fear
(Tzion)
is from the revelation of the loftiness of Ein Sof that is above worlds, which is drawn down through Torah and mitzvos.
And based on this,
the precision in the verse "Praise Yerushalayim, Havayah; laud your G-d, Tzion"
(that regarding Yerushalayim it says Havayah and regarding Tzion it says Elokim)
is also regarding the matter of Yerushalayim and Tzion in the service of man.
For it is known
regarding the matter of Havayah and Elokim,
that Elokim is the light that fills
(light that is commensurate with the worlds)
and Havayah is the encompassing light
(light that is above worlds).
And from this it is understood,
that lower fear is related to Elokim and higher fear to Havayah,
and nevertheless,
regarding Yerushalayim
(lower fear)
it says Havayah, and regarding Tzion
(higher fear)
it says Elokim.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section elaborates on the two aspects of contemplation that lead to lower fear, explaining that all creation stems from the lowest level, the world of speech called "the city of our G-d."

translations.translation: And the explanation of the superiority of higher fear
(Tzion)
in more detail,
will be understood by prefacing what is explained in the aforementioned maamar "Shivchi,"
that in the contemplation that brings to lower fear
(Yerushalayim)
there are two matters.
The contemplation of His greatness in the creation itself,
both regarding the matter of "how
great are Your works, Havayah" and regarding the matter of "how
great are Your works, Havayah."
And the contemplation that all coming-into-being
(of the multitude of creations and the great ones of the creations)
is only from the very last level.
As it is stated,
"Great is Havayah and exceedingly praised in the city of our G-d," and our sages said,
"When is He great? When He is in the city of our G-d,"
that His greatness as it is in itself is beyond our comprehension,
and that which we know His greatness through the creation of the worlds is like it is in the city of our G-d, which is the world of speech.
For just as a city in its simple sense is a collection of many houses, and a house is from many stones,
so too is it in spirituality,
that letters are called stones, and the words formed from the combination of several letters are called houses
[as it is brought in Sefer Yetzirah,
"two stones build two houses, three stones build six houses"]
and the world of speech
(in its totality)
is called the city of our G-d.
And just as stones
[and likewise the houses and the city made from the stones]
are inanimate,
the very last level among the inanimate, vegetative, animate, and speaking,
so too is it regarding the world of speech from which all worlds come into being,
that it is the very last level.
And this is "and the word of Havayah from Yerushalayim,"
that the word of Havayah that brings into being, enlivens, and sustains all creations is from Yerushalayim,
the city of our G-d,
the level of inanimate.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the contemplation that creation is only from the lowest level leads to the completeness of fear, connecting the two interpretations of Yerushalayim as the world of speech and as the perfection of fear.

translations.translation: And it can be said,
that what is explained in the maamar, that the contemplation that brings to lower fear
(Yerushalayim)
is
(not only in the greatness within creation,
but also)
in this, that the coming-into-being is only from the very last level,
is,
because Yerushalayim is "fear complete,"
the perfection of fear.
And in order for fear
(the self-nullification)
to be complete,
it is through the contemplation that creations do not occupy space.
And this is the connection of the two interpretations
(matters)
regarding Yerushalayim – that Yerushalayim is the world of speech and that Yerushalayim is the perfection of fear – that through the contemplation of "the word of Havayah from Yerushalayim,"
that the coming-into-being of all worlds is
(only)
from the level of Yerushalayim
(the world of speech)
which is a level of inanimate relative to the levels above it,
through this one will come to the perfection of fear.
